en.sup: Supplied in English. The Hebrew sets 'this' beside its description without a verb.

01.r: Points ahead to the explanation that follows.

02.r: What follows is a statement about the levy: what it was raised for.
02.n: Literally 'the word of'. The brief's lexicon lists 'matter, case, business' among this noun's senses, and that is its use here. The KJV and ASV say 'the reason of'; the DRC 'the sum of', likely following its Latin source.

03.r: The drafted workers who built Solomon's projects.
03.n: BDB: a body of task-workers for public service, formed by levy upon the people, and it names Solomon's levy. Gesenius gives 'tribute', the sense behind Geneva's and YLT's 'the tribute'. The DRC's 'the expenses' turns the levy into money; the BSB's 'the forced labor' matches BDB.

04.r: Joins the levy to the act of raising it.

05.r: Solomon called the workers up for service.
05.n: The causative of the verb 'go up', 'made go up', the same verb used for raising the levy in 1 Kings 5:13. YLT keeps the picture: 'hath lifted up'.

07.r: The king who raised the levy.

08.r: The purpose of the levy: building works.
08.n: Gesenius: to build, to erect, as a house, a temple, a city, walls, defences: every kind of building in this list.

09.r: Marks 'the house of the LORD' as the first thing built.
09.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'the house of'.

11.r: The personal name of Israel's God.
11.n: The KJV, Geneva and DRC say 'the Lord', the BSB 'the LORD' in small capitals, the ASV and YLT 'Jehovah', and the JPS 'HaShem' ('the Name').

12.r: 'And', with the object marker before the next item.
12.n: The object marker with 'and' is repeated before every item in the list; only the 'and' has an English equivalent.

13.n: The Hebrew says only 'his house'; 'own' marks that it is Solomon's, not the LORD's. The BSB says 'his own palace'.

15.r: A filled-in earthwork that was part of Jerusalem's fortifications.
15.n: Gesenius: properly a rampart or mound, built up and filled in with stones and earth, here part of the citadel of Jerusalem, citing this verse. The BSB translates it, 'the supporting terraces'; the other versions keep the name.

17.r: The defensive wall round the city.
17.n: Gesenius: a wall, generally the wall of a town.

20.r: A city in the north that Solomon fortified.
20.n: Gesenius: a town in the tribe of Naphtali, fortified by Solomon, citing this verse.

22.r: A fortified city overlooking the plain of Esdraelon.
22.n: Gesenius: a fortified city of the Manassites, formerly a royal city of the Canaanites. The brief's lexicon links its name to the New Testament 'Armageddon'.

24.r: A city on the border of Ephraim, the last in the list.
24.n: The brief's lexicon: a Levitical city on the border of Ephraim.
